heroText: Oulu is a northern Finnish tech and cycling city on the Gulf of Bothnia, with beaches, islands and winter routines built into daily life. Start at the Market Square Policeman, visit Pikisaari, then head to Nallikari beach or Hupisaaret Islands. Oulu Airport is close and connects the city with Helsinki and northern routes.

areas.name: Oulu centre
areas.text: The centre is best for first stays, with restaurants, shops, the market square and station access close together.

areas.name: Pikisaari
areas.text: Pikisaari is an island district with old wooden buildings, studios and a quieter waterside feel.

areas.name: Nallikari
areas.text: Nallikari is the beach and resort area, best for summer stays, families and sea views.

areas.name: Tuira
areas.text: Tuira sits north of the centre with local services, river access and practical apartment stays.

airports.name: Oulu Airport (OUL)
airports.text: Oulu Airport is southwest of the city in Oulunsalo; buses, taxis and transfers connect it with the centre.

airportTransfer.value: 20-30 min by taxi or airport bus to central Oulu
airportTransfer.distance: about 15 km southwest of the centre

stayOverview: Choose Oulu centre for restaurants and transport, Pikisaari for atmosphere and water, Nallikari for beach and resort stays, or Tuira for apartments and a more local base north of the river.
hotelIntro: Oulu is practical and spread around waterways. Central hotels work for most visits, while Nallikari is seasonal and family-focused, Pikisaari is more atmospheric, and Tuira suits longer stays.
rentalCars: A car helps for Bothnian coast and nature trips, but Oulu's centre and cycle network are easy without one.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Stay centrally for winter visits, when short walks to restaurants and transport matter more than beach access.

travelTips.title: Cycling
travelTips.text: Oulu is serious about year-round cycling, but winter visitors should dress for cold wind and icy surfaces.

travelTips.title: Beach season
travelTips.text: Nallikari is best in summer; outside warm months it is more about walks and sea air.

travelTips.title: Day trip
travelTips.text: Keep one side-trip day flexible from Oulu, then choose it only after checking transport frequency and opening hours.

history.label: Origins
history.text: The city is named after the river Oulujoki, which originates in the lake Oulujärvi.
Following the Treaty of Nöteborg in 1323, the status of Oulu was disputed in its ownership, as both the Novgorod Republic and the Kingdom of Sweden held much influence.
In 1345, the Swedish annexed territory up to the Kemi River for the Diocese of Turku.
In 1375, the Novgorodians built a defensive castle which was later captured by the Swedish forces in 1377.
In 1531, the city was granted permission to act as a trading post.
In 1590, the Oulu Castle was built by the Swedes and in 1595, the Treaty of Teusina firmly established Sweden's control over Oulu.
The city was founded on 8 April 1605 by King Charles IX of Sweden, and granted city privileges in 1610.
In 1765, Oulu received township rights granting them to trade outside of Sweden.
Oulu was the capital of the Province of Oulu from 1776 to 2009.
In 1822, a major fire destroyed much of the city, especially the city centre as most of the city was made from wood.
The Oulu Cathedral was built in 1832 to his designs, with the spire being finished in 1844.
The city was the site of the Battle of Oulu on 3 February 1918 between the Whites and the Reds during the Finnish Civil War.

history.label: Modern city
history.text: One possible source is a word in the Sami language meaning 'flood water', but there are other suggestions.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: During the Åland War, part of the Crimean War, Oulu's harbour was raided by the British fleet, who destroyed ships and burned tar houses, leading to international criticism.
